title: Business Texting for HubSpot — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Business Texting Tools That Work With HubSpot
description: Salesmsg, Aircall, and Calilio compared for small teams that text customers from HubSpot: prices, what gets logged, workflow triggers, and calling.
h1: Business texting that works with HubSpot
dek: Three tools that let a small team send and receive business texts and keep every message on the HubSpot record, so nobody texts a customer from a personal phone again.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This is for a small sales or service team, often three to ten people, whose customers answer texts faster than email, and who keep contacts and deals in {{link:hubspot}}.
The problem these tools solve is simple: texts sent from personal phones never reach the CRM, so the next person to pick up the account has no idea what was said.

Pick Salesmsg if most of the work is texting, and you want HubSpot workflows to send texts on their own. Pick Aircall if the team mostly makes calls and texting is a side channel. Pick Calilio if you want calls and texts on HubSpot timelines and the per-user price matters most.

Start with which channel carries the work. If the team texts all day, a texting-first tool with workflow triggers saves the most time. If the team is on the phone all day, buy the phone system and use its texting.
Then count seats honestly. A minimum license count or a per-seat add-on changes the math more than the headline price does for a team this size.
Finally, check the compliance basics: who registers your numbers for business texting, how opt-outs reach HubSpot, and whether texts to some countries cost extra.
Clean phone number fields first. Texting tools match conversations to contacts by number, so a mix of formats creates duplicate contacts on day one.
Agree on one property that marks a contact as opted out of texts, and make sure the tool you pick writes to it.
